mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate indicates monetary easing, which can lead to increased borrowing and investment, thereby driving up S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns despite falling FEDFUNDS, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) above a threshold signals strong consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If HOUST increases but S&P 500 returns are negative, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment (UNRATE) coupled with falling employment (PAYEMS) indicates economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If both UNRATE and PAYEMS signals are positive but S&P 500 returns are negative, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Growth in industrial production (INDPRO) during an expansion regime signals increased economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO grows but S&P 500 returns are negative, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS) increase borrowing costs, reducing investment and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS are high but S&P 500 returns are positive, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Real federal spending (RSAFS) growth indicates increased demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS grows but S&P 500 returns are negative, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Improving labor market (UNRATE and PAYEMS) signals economic strength, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If labor market improves but S&P 500 returns are negative, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below a threshold signals reduced supply, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO is below threshold but S&P 500 returns are positive, the hypothesis is falsified.
